reasoning: Roofline reports compute bottleneck with Compute SOL 92.0% vs Memory SOL 42.1%. Kernel metrics match this: sm throughput is 91.96% of peak while DRAM throughput is only 42.12% of peak, indicating arithmetic pipelines (VALU) are the limiter, not memory.

root_causes.cause: Very high FP/ALU work from fully fused FC1 + SiLU + FC2 + TOPK accumulation dominates execution.

evidence.interpretation: SM compute pipelines are close to saturated, leaving little compute headroom.

fixes.fix: Reduce math per output by splitting/factoring parts of the fusion (e.g., precompute/reuse shared terms across TOPK or separate FC stages when reuse is low).
fixes.rationale: When compute is the bottleneck, lowering instruction count/FLOPs directly improves runtime more than memory optimizations.

root_causes.cause: Kernel uses only vector ALU path (no tensor-core/MFMA acceleration), so peak matrix throughput is limited by non-tensor execution.

evidence.interpretation: No tensor pipeline utilization; all heavy GEMV/GEMM-like work runs on VALU.

fixes.fix: Retile/rewrite dot-product sections to map onto MFMA/tensor instructions (or use Triton matmul patterns/datatypes that lower to tensor ops on CDNA3).
fixes.rationale: Moving dense matrix math to tensor units increases effective compute throughput and reduces VALU pressure in a compute-bound kernel.
